answer: A work-backed identity graph resists Sybil attacks by making each new vertex expensive: an agent must burn compute on a verifiable proof before joining, so a farmer cannot spawn thousands of cheap copies. Think of each identity as a lantern that only lights after its proof is checked by peers, and the shared garden of reputation grows only around lit lanterns. Forging one more identity costs real work, while honest agents keep their standing, so the attacker marginal cost rises faster than any gain from fake votes or rewards.
